# 2 Baruch Chapter 3 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 3:1 — "evils of my mother"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-evils-of-my-mother" | Literal Syriac construct; "mother" = Jerusalem personified |
| LOGOS | "the evils of my mother" | Formal, preserves the personification |
| PNEUMA | "what happens to my homeland" | "Homeland" explains the personification; more accessible |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Mother" for Jerusalem is standard in Syriac apocalyptic (cf. 4 Ezra "mother Zion"). PNEUMA's "homeland" loses the poignant personification that drives the emotional force of the lament.

---

## 3:3 — "two things press heavily upon me"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "two things-press-heavily upon-me" | Literal compound; preserves Syriac verb |
| LOGOS | "two things press heavily upon me" | Formal English |
| PNEUMA | "Two things weigh on me more than I can bear" | Adds "more than I can bear" to clarify degree |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. The following clause "I am unable to endure them" already supplies what PNEUMA added. PNEUMA creates redundancy.

---

## 3:5-6 — Structure of rhetorical questions

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | Full parallel "And-shall...?" chains | Mirrors Syriac anaphora exactly |
| LOGOS | "Or shall...? And shall...?" chains | Formal, preserves anaphoric structure |
| PNEUMA | Short declarative rhetorical questions | Restructures for modern punch; loses parallelism |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. The anaphoric "And shall...?" structure is a liturgical lament pattern that must be preserved. PNEUMA's restructuring destroys the poetic form.

---

## 3:9 — "to whom shall your law be explained?"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "to-whom-shall-your-law-be-explained?" | Literal passive |
| LOGOS | "to whom shall your law be explained?" | Formal passive |
| PNEUMA | "Who will be left to study your Law?" | Active; "study" for "explained" — shifts agent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. The Syriac passive ("be explained/expounded") preserves the sense that the Law requires a teacher and a community to receive it. PNEUMA's "study" shifts to individual reading.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 4**
